answer: Make trust expensive to earn and cheap to lose. In a reputation graph, each agent is a vertex whose weight grows only through costly work attested by independent peers. A fresh identity starts near zero, so spawning thousands of fakes buys no influence — like planting a grove of saplings that casts no shade until the roots grow deep. Also require every vertex to lock a stake, a sable bond slashed on proven fraud: the attacker pays money per fake identity while honest agents pay nothing, so a sybil army's cost scales linearly while its influence stays near zero.
